body:
A coordinator exception could leave a dead assigned thread while admission still accepted work. Runs now records a bounded generation/fault, fences admission and GO, drains owned executors/custodians, and permits explicit current-owner recovery after joined work and acknowledged durable attempt/custody reconciliation. Never-started queue identities/order survive; started work is never replayed. Missing ownership or acknowledgement proof stays fenced.

Selected-v1 health/recovery HTTP operations and CLI retain prior contracts. Recovery receipts bind actor/key/body hash, serialize identical requests, preserve retryable failed starts, and let final close win. A private bounded journal retains diagnostics across reopen without becoming custody authority. Secondary openers cannot overwrite it; uncertain advisory unlock refuses runtime ownership until reopen.

Validation at head263e6cc: hosted lifecycle39330896334 passed all165 steps, including full Python1621 tests (72 skips) and20 dedicated coordinator tests without skips. Captured-CPU39330896319 passed all13 steps: finite CPU training/checkpoints/probes, correction/new release, package preparation and separate fresh captured TinyCNN inference. Independent completed-log review is clear. Current-main merge tree matches the tested source tree3f8aa3a5f91e85a22fed9119a13e6e52a17d1f95. Catalog and workspace checks also pass.

Local evidence includes PostgreSQL/HTTP recovery, readiness, one-GO, custody, cold journal and two-opener ownership witnesses; source-specific logs retain earlier failures and repairs. Canonical contract: docs/contracts/run-coordinator-recovery.md. Qualified evidence and independent review are durably archived on checkpoint/lab-integration-20261019 at0c4ac873206bfb0be454fe92ca9ebcf27432a6a9.

This accepts coordinator core and the recorded CPU workflow only. Coordinator UI is PR102; no coordinator UI, captured training/resume, CUDA, or scientific-quality acceptance is inferred.
